papers.title: Optical clocks at sea
papers.access: Full publisher HTML; supplementary DOCX opened
papers.sections_reviewed: Main; Methods entire; Extended Data 1–5 captions; supplementary Potential Correlations and Mobile Platforms
papers.defensible_result: Three engineered iodine clocks operated at sea; pairwise PICKLES–EPIC instability was 8e-15 at 100000 s without drift removal, with independent NIST comparisons before deployment.

objections.claim_under_test: Each sea clock independently accrued <300 ps/day absolute timing error
objections.evidence: Long-time sea result is pairwise, normalized by sqrt(2) assuming equal contributions; no independent reference at sea. Supplement provides land sensitivity tests and argues correlations small, rather than measuring absolute shipboard timing.
objections.locator: Main following Fig.3; Supplement Potential Correlations in At-Sea Data
objections.consequence: Preserves pairwise stability; individual absolute holdover is inferred and assumption-dependent.

objections.claim_under_test: Continuous autonomous operation and 35 L describe the entire deployed installation
objections.evidence: VIPER restarted once after external power-supply software fault; displayed record begins after restart. Three-clock metrology installation occupied 23 U with supplies/laptops/UPS.
objections.locator: Main RIMPAC deployment; Methods RIMPAC test setup; Fig.3a
objections.consequence: Qualifies uptime and platform burden; does not undermine clock stability.

papers.what_survives: Robust mobile optical-clock engineering and strong laboratory-reference performance survive.
papers.what_would_resolve: Independent diverse reference at sea, direct holdover residuals with specified initialization, full installation SWaP and uptime logs.
papers.verdict: Strong field result; do not equate Allan-deviation-derived holdover with independently observed absolute error.

papers.title: Quantum-assured magnetic navigation
papers.access: Full local arXiv HTML including tables
papers.sections_reviewed: Entire main text; Table1; Appendix Table2
papers.defensible_result: Reported map-aided navigation improves endpoint error over strategic-grade INS across aircraft and ground trials, including onboard sensors with scalar airspeed aiding.

objections.claim_under_test: 22 m and 46x are demonstrated complete-GNSS-denial performance
objections.evidence: Table1 assigns both headline endpoints to 3D-velocity-aided configurations; Fig.4b explicitly singles out scalar-airspeed configuration as complete GNSS denial. Source of 3D velocity is not specified in reviewed version.
objections.locator: Table1; Fig.1 caption; Demonstration of MagNav; Fig.4
objections.consequence: Cannot assign best numbers to GNSS-free velocity aiding. This is missing provenance, not proof that GNSS leaked. Scalar-airspeed endpoints 515/566 m remain.

objections.claim_under_test: Quantum hardware rather than map-aiding/software causes superiority
objections.evidence: INS alone is comparator; no equivalent conventional-magnetometer MagNav ablation. Algorithm coefficients, likelihood and data are not supplied in sufficient detail for independent reconstruction.
objections.locator: Q-CTRL magnetic denoising and map-matching algorithms; Discussion optimal sensor architecture
objections.consequence: System-level advantage survives; quantum-specific advantage and independent reproducibility unestablished.

objections.claim_under_test: Cold start means unaided global localization and real-time closed-loop flight demonstrated
objections.evidence: Cold start refers to platform magnetic model; initial position supplied, tolerated errors reported up to4 km. Iterative filter is designed for real-time; discussion calls correction quasi-real-time; live flight-management integration not documented.
objections.locator: Algorithms; Fig.6; Discussion
objections.consequence: Preserves causal algorithm claim, restricts initialization and operational claims. No evidence of whole-flight smoothing was found.

objections.claim_under_test: Endpoint minima establish continuous navigation accuracy or indefinite boundedness
objections.evidence: 22m is best final position, 46x is endpoint ratio; maps have coverage and relief limitations explicitly acknowledged.
objections.locator: Abstract; Table1; Discussion final paragraphs
objections.consequence: Cannot substitute endpoints for RMS/percentiles or infer global robustness.

papers.what_survives: Promising multisensor map-navigation trial evidence, especially scalar-airspeed onboard results.
papers.what_would_resolve: Velocity-input provenance, held-out routes, full error distributions, algorithm/data release, conventional MagNav comparator and logged live integration.
papers.verdict: Promising preprint, with headline aiding and comparator qualifications.

papers.title: GNSS-free quantum gravity-aided navigation
papers.access: Full local arXiv HTML including Fig.2 caption
papers.defensible_result: A reported GNSS-withheld gravity-aided chain reduces terminal inertial error from26 km to4.0–4.1 km on83 km route; separate GNSS-aided survey supports repeatable gravity recovery.

objections.claim_under_test: Nautical-mile DRMS and ~1nmi bounded positioning over entire evaluation
objections.evidence: Abstract says DRMS; Fig.2 caption explicitly says1nmi band is not a reported DRMS statistic. Results give2.2nmi terminal error and1nmi only first38 of45nmi; Discussion describes~1nmi bound over evaluation.
objections.locator: Abstract; Fig.2 caption; Results Quantum navigation; Discussion second paragraph
objections.consequence: Internal reporting inconsistency invalidates specific full-route1nmi/DRMS characterization, not demonstrated error reduction.

objections.claim_under_test: 70x drift and0.16mGal repeatability establish mobile navigation advantage over classical systems
objections.evidence: 70x is an Allan-deviation ratio at80000s in56h stationary laboratory record;0.16mGal is mean inter-trace difference, whereas spatial residual RMS0.67mGal. Classical-only ablation omits atomic bias correction without optimized classical drift calibration.
objections.locator: Fig.7; Methods hybridization; Results Strapdown; Discussion classical benchmarks
objections.consequence: Preserves bias-stabilization evidence but not70x mobile navigation improvement or0.16mGal spatial accuracy; authors acknowledge superior classical survey benchmarks.

objections.claim_under_test: Gimbaled-versus-strapdown equivalence holds through roughest sea conditions
objections.evidence: Gimbaled coastal runs typically Sea States2–3; strapdown typically1; only northbound gimbaled run samples largest motion. Noisy northbound trace excluded from other traces’ reference ensembles.
objections.locator: Methods Maritime details; Methods gravity signal; Fig.4 caption
objections.consequence: Comparison valid in overlapping motion range; unequal exposure/selection limits broader robustness inference.

objections.claim_under_test: Autonomous live closed navigation and fully specified initial conditions established
objections.evidence: Recorded raw IMU is independently mechanized and both estimates share initial state; quantitative initialization uncertainty/source and live closed-loop timing are not detailed. Paper explicitly calls long-duration fully closed campaign future work.
objections.locator: Results Quantum navigation; Methods Gravity-aided navigation; Discussion future work
objections.consequence: No basis to allege hidden GNSS; insufficient to establish cold-start or online autonomy. GNSS-aided survey branch explicitly separate.

papers.what_survives: GNSS-withheld map-aiding and hybrid mobile gravimetry survive, subject to reported rather than reproduced chain independence.
papers.what_would_resolve: Correct DRMS/endpoint language; publish trajectory/error statistics and initialization; live long-duration trial; matched-motion and optimized classical comparisons.
papers.verdict: Useful preprint with consequential metric inconsistency; application superiority remains unproved.

papers.title: Quantum sensing for gravity cartography
papers.access: Full14-page publisher PDF; image review Extended Data Tables1–2
papers.sections_reviewed: All main results; full Methods; Extended Data captions and Tables1–2
papers.defensible_result: Outdoor quantum gradiometry detects a known tunnel anomaly consistent with site model; test-mass control agrees205±13.1E with202E prediction.

objections.claim_under_test: Blind tunnel discovery and unique depth/geometry determination
objections.evidence: Known tunnel/site supported by CAD/GPR/topographic model. Inference assumes buried cuboid, informative density prior−1.80±0.10g/cm3; depth1.89−0.59/+2.3m broad and parameter ambiguity explicit. Horizontal prior sigma4m is broad, so accurate location is not simply fixed by tight prior.
objections.locator: pp591–592; Methods Inference; Extended Data Table2
objections.consequence: Survives detection/localization on characterized site; does not establish blind unknown-target discrimination.

objections.claim_under_test: SNR8 is8-sigma hypothesis evidence and 15min mapping achieved
objections.evidence: SNR estimated150E approximate signal divided17.9E mean point uncertainty; survey uses600shots per measurement, repeats, interleaved base stations and line drift subtraction.15min/SNR3 explicitly conditional future calculation.
objections.locator: p593; Methods Survey practice pp7–8 PDF
objections.consequence: No false-alarm/null-model probability follows from SNR; projected survey speed not measured total time.

objections.claim_under_test: Statistical superiority means superior practical commercial survey performance
objections.evidence: Authors state survey repeatability similar to commercial gravimeters and systematic-limited; table gives<26E yaw-related point-to-point effects and<43E magnetic bound limited by calibration resolution.
objections.locator: p593; Extended Data Table1
objections.consequence: Preserves differential noise rejection but not blanket operational superiority or exhaustive systematic immunity.

papers.what_survives: Convincing known-target field demonstration with meaningful test-mass control and openly described processing.
papers.what_would_resolve: Blind sites with target-absent controls, matched-time classical survey, prior/model sensitivity tests and complete survey elapsed time.
papers.verdict: Strong scientific/engineering result; blind detection, geometry certainty and faster survey extrapolations restricted.

papers.title: Demonstration of Quantum Advantage in Microwave Quantum Radar
papers.access: Full14-page arXiv v2 PDF including Methods; journal version of record not examined; numerical criticism applies only to arXiv v2. Rounding/averaging provenance of the discrepant printed denominator is not documented in this version.
papers.defensible_result: Joint microwave signal-idler measurement reports Q1.2(1) relative to modeled optimal coherent-state bound in cold, known-target binary detection experiment.

objections.claim_under_test: General practical radar advantage
objections.evidence: Position, speed and reflectivity assumed known; target coaxial delay/filter at15mK, delay86ns; added thermal noise switched on only after state preparation.
objections.locator: pp1–3; Fig.1; Methods B3
objections.consequence: Does not demonstrate unknown-target search/ranging or warm open-air operation. These restrictions are explicit, not concealed.

objections.claim_under_test: Quoted uncertainty establishes robust advantage after all tuning/calibration choices
objections.evidence: Methods F says photon-number uncertainties mostly statistical, omit protocol imperfections, and classical bound propagation assumes independent calibrations. Gain and outcome weights selected to maximize E; no separate held-out tuning evaluation specified.
objections.locator: Eq.1; Figs3–4; Methods E–F pp11–12
objections.consequence: Modest excess needs systematic and selection-robust validation. This is not evidence advantage vanishes. Optimal classical bound is a strong comparator, not straw man.

objections.claim_under_test: Printed numerical classical bound is self-consistent
objections.evidence: p4 prints Ecl2.1(1)e-5, but printed kappa0.0302,NS0.0353,NN10.8 and formula kappaNS/(4NN) give approximately2.47e-5. E2.9e-5 divided latter gives1.18, consistent Q1.2; divided2.1e-5 gives1.38. Later p4 Ecl=kappaNS/NN also omits factor4.
objections.locator: pp1,3–4; Methods F Eq.8
objections.consequence: Reporting/arithmetic error warrants correction; does not itself refute Q1.2, which agrees with parameter-derived denominator.

objections.claim_under_test: Full model quantitatively explains observed excess
objections.evidence: Authors explicitly note model systematically underestimates Q with origin unresolved, possible measurement model issue.
objections.locator: p4 Fig.4 discussion
objections.consequence: Limits mechanistic quantitative confidence, not independent demonstration by itself.

papers.what_survives: Narrow quantum-illumination proof of principle with joint receiver and nontrivial optimal-classical comparator.
papers.what_would_resolve: Correct denominator text; systematic calibration covariance and independent tuning/test sets; direct error-vs-attempt curves for claimed exponent.
papers.verdict: Credible narrow result; quantitative uncertainty and reporting require care, deployment not shown.

papers.title: Performance of antenna-based and Rydberg quantum RF sensors in the electrically small regime
papers.access: Full published PDF from https://inspirehep.net/files/ac16594fd5658d98b52993e9f1437037 ; Eq7/10 visually checked. Supplement code not obtained: publisher inaccessible.
papers.defensible_result: Model comparison properly includes active high-impedance classical receivers and predicts present warm-vapour REIT sensitivity worse than amplified small dipoles.

objections.claim_under_test: Printed input-referred active-noise Eq7 and quantum-limit Eq10 follow definitions
objections.evidence: Eq7 multiplies amplifier noise by voltage-divider squared; input-referred amplifier noise should divide by squared transfer, while antenna Johnson input noise remains at input. Limit Ramp→0 gives zero printed NEV despite lost signal. Separately definitions Q=omega*tau*exp(−tau*Gamma), Vout_noise²=tau/N imply NEVin²=exp(2tauGamma)/(N*omega²*tau); at tau=1/(2Gamma) this is2eGamma/(N*omega²), but Eq10 prints2Gamma/(e*N*omega²).
objections.locator: Published p144002-3, Eq7; paragraph defining Q; Eqs9–10 (PDFp4, visually checked)
objections.consequence: Concrete internal equation inconsistencies; numerical-curve impact unresolved without supplement. Does not establish reversal of Fig3 qualitative ordering.

objections.claim_under_test: Ideal RSQL forecast establishes realizable sensor sensitivity or full-system size superiority
objections.evidence: RSQL assumes tightly packed cold atoms, optimized~1e8 atoms in1cm3, interaction shift cap1MHz; authors call ideal sensor likely physically unrealizable and note collective effects.1cm comparison is sensing region, not lasers/control/vacuum.
objections.consequence: Ideal sensitivity is model-dependent benchmark, not achieved performance or full-platform SWaP.

objections.claim_under_test: Lower intrinsic noise automatically improves outdoor reception
objections.evidence: Assumes equal dipole directivity3/2 and same external noise; both ideal curves below atmospheric background.
objections.consequence: Improvement requires appropriate external-noise regime; not a generic communications advantage.

papers.what_survives: Valuable correction to weak passive classical baselines; near-term active classical comparator remains compelling under stated assumptions.
papers.what_would_resolve: Author correction and static inspection of supplementary plot code; matched-bandwidth full-system experiments; feasible atom-density/decoherence validation.
papers.verdict: Useful benchmark, but two printed algebraic inconsistencies demand qualification before numerical ideal limits are reused.
